summary: Deaf touches an index finger to the ear and then to the mouth (or mouth then ear). Both orders are standard.
movement: Touch the ear, then touch near the corner of the mouth
steps: Touch the tip of your index finger to your ear, just in front of it.
Move it to touch the side of your mouth or chin.
Either direction, ear-to-mouth or mouth-to-ear, is correct.
note: Say 'Deaf,' not 'hearing impaired.' Most Deaf people dislike 'hearing impaired' because it defines them by what they lack. Deaf with a capital D refers to cultural identity and ASL use.
mistakes: Touching the ear and stopping. Both points are part of the sign.

faq.q: Is it okay to sign DEAF to describe someone?
faq.a: Yes. It is the standard, respectful sign. The one to avoid is the old HEARING-IMPAIRED construction.
